exposure: Time elapsed from onset of symptoms to diagnosis
cohort: The study included 583 pregnancies from 378 women with IBD identified from a tertiary IBD center in Denmark between 2008 and 2021, comparing those with new onset IBD during pregnancy to those diagnosed prior to pregnancy.
finding: Birth outcomes in pregnancies affected by pregnancy-onset IBD (PO-IBD) were comparable to those in women diagnosed with IBD prior to pregnancy, despite women with PO-IBD receiving more corticosteroids and biologics.
mod_finding: The study found no significant difference in the rate of caesarean section between pregnancies affected by PO-IBD and controls.
